raw_response:
I am seventy-three years old this year. I have been farming this land in Quzhou since I was a young man, more than fifty years. My father taught me, and now I do what I have always done, with some small changes I have seen from my neighbors.

I have about ten mu of land in total. Eight mu I use for wheat and maize, one after the other — that is what everyone here does. The other two mu I plant with cotton. I keep the cotton because if the grain prices are bad, the cotton still brings some cash, and my wife can help pick it. At my age I cannot take big risks.

For the wheat, I will plant in early October, after rotary tillage. I buy improved seed from the shop in town — I used to save my own, but the shop seed grows better now. Before planting I spread about one hundred jin per mu of compound fertilizer, the general kind. That is about what my neighbor Lao Zhang uses. I also put down some urea, maybe forty or fifty jin per mu, because last year I skimped on nitrogen and the wheat turned yellow at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading if it is dry. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice — the aphids always come. I expect about one thousand jin per mu, which is five hundred kilograms.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, there is almost no time. I plant the maize the same week, no-tillage, directly into the stubble. I buy Denghai 605 hybrid seed — everyone says it is good, and my nephew got over one thousand jin per mu with it last year. For maize I use about eighty jin per mu of compound fertilizer at planting. That is all, no topdressing — I am too busy and too tired by then. I irrigate twice, once right after planting if it does not rain, and once at the big trumpet leaf stage. I spray three times total for weeds and borers. I hope for about one thousand jin per mu, maybe a bit more if the rain is good.

The cotton I plant in late April, after rotary tillage. I buy improved seed. I use about one hundred jin per mu of compound fertilizer as basal. Cotton needs water but not too much — I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll stage. But the pests are terrible. I have to spray almost every week during summer, fifteen times or more, for bollworm and aphids. It is a lot of work and costs money, but the cotton price has been steady. I expect about five hundred to six hundred jin of seed cotton per mu.

I am getting old. My knees hurt. I do everything a little slower than before. But I know this land. I will stick with what works.
